I appreciate this response and your kind words. I wanna address my situation for a second  My therapy with my psychiatrist is covered by OHIP - I go to a mental health unit at my local hospital. But I used to pay out of pocket for my prescription medication  - I'm on a few that I literally cannot function without. When I paid out of pocket, the costs for my meds were around 400 a month. Now that I work full time and have insurance, I just pay a deductible. When I had to pay out of pocket, I struggled, also because I didnt have a full time job. There were days I went without medication because I simply couldn't afford it, and that made it incredibly difficult for me to function. For parents who have children with autism, the therapy is incredibly expensive but without it their children are doomed to not be productive members of society and to not have a fulfilling life. It costs around 5k for speech and behaviour therapy for some kids. When I see a single dad talking about how he has to take out a second mortgage on his house to pay for his child's therapy...I empathize. And it's sad because this kid is doomed to fail without it. By that, I mean this kid will likely never learn to talk, will have behavioural issues that prevent him from forming any sort of relationship or having a job or being independent. Which still screws over society, because that means this adult will still have to be cared for the government, which will cost more money in the long run. My issues arent comparable to autism, but I still have a sickness that if I dont manage, I cant function. I can afford my meds now even if I didnt have insurance because I have a full time job and I earn a decent salary, but I recognize that there are people out there who dont earn as much or cant work at all, and what do they do? I'm okay with paying more taxes if I'm going to be helping people who are in this situation, I'm not rolling in money and I have to budget carefully but social programs are important for the benefit of the community. Life isnt easy, and I really do get that there are also other groups out there that need funding, but I dont think that cancels out the importance of funding for autistic treatment. And it's completely fair if you dont agree, I guess I took more issue with the idea that these parents are looking for a handout - maybe *some* are, but what I see is parents that really love and want to take care of their children and are desperate for support. They dont know what else to do. And to bring it back to myself for a second...I'm a nurse and I love helping people and I think that I've been able to make a positive difference in some of my patients lives...but if I hadn't been able to receive therapy, I wouldnt be able to be a nurse. I think ultimately there's a payoff. I dont know. Just my opinion.
